title: Bolt vs Replit
summary: Compare two AI app-building workflows by project fit, handoff, operating ownership and the real cost of a working release.

sections.heading: Start with the project shape
paragraphs: Bolt's reviewed profile documents a JavaScript web-app path and an Expo mobile path. Replit's profile describes an AI agent for building applications. Confirm the actual framework, backend, data store and deployment target your project needs before treating either scope as a fit.

sections.heading: Test the handoff
paragraphs: Build the same small feature, then perform a clean checkout or export and run the project using documented steps. Record what remains tied to the original hosted workspace, including environment variables, databases and deployment configuration.

sections.heading: Estimate a live service separately
paragraphs: Replit's public sources list USD 20/month with monthly billing and USD 18/month equivalent billed annually. These are base-plan amounts, not a complete production budget; include runtime, database, model usage, backups and support only when each item has evidence for the intended plan.

pros.text: Bolt documents a JavaScript-based web-app workflow and a separate Expo path for mobile apps.
Replit describes Agent as a plain-language workflow that plans, creates, checks, fixes and deploys applications.

cons.text: Bolt's documented web-app path is JavaScript-based, so confirm the exact framework and dependencies before selecting it for a project.
Replit documents repository backup, selected project imports and in-platform checkpoints; these do not establish a complete portable app export.

faqs.question: What application paths does Bolt document?
faqs.answer: The official introduction describes JavaScript-based web frameworks and an Expo route for mobile applications; verify your specific stack before starting.

faqs.question: What does Replit document for code import and recovery?
faqs.answer: Replit lists GitHub, Bitbucket and ZIP imports and an App-managed backup that can restore the repository's commit history. Provider-specific imports may require separate secrets, data or service setup. Agent checkpoints support rollback inside Replit; the docs do not establish a complete portable export or migration. No import or restore was tested.

faqs.question: Does Replit's AI Integrations page establish local-model support for Replit Agent?
faqs.answer: Not from the reviewed docs. Replit describes AI Integrations as provider API access configured for the apps being built: managed credentials are billed to Replit credits at provider prices, while a developer's own API key is billed by the provider. A separate Model selector page describes model choice for Replit Agent itself. Neither page documents a local model or endpoint for Replit Agent, so local-model support remains unverified rather than being marked unsupported. No account, endpoint, integration or model was tested.

verdict: Choose after a clean handoff and operating-cost trial. The current evidence is not sufficient to declare a universal winner or a fixed total application cost.
bestFor: Indie builders comparing a quick application workflow with the cost of owning its production lifecycle
notFor: Projects with unverified portability, data-residency or production-budget requirements
migration: For Replit, use the documented Git/import paths for code, inventory secrets, database records, production data and connected services separately, then prove an independent deployment. No Replit project was exported or restored.
gaps: Replit's public monthly and annual-billed Core base prices are recorded; confirm account eligibility, location-based checkout taxes, included usage and full application costs before a budget comparison.
No clean export, independent deployment, account-level geography selection or performance test has been performed.
